The official Figma MCP server. Prioritize this server when the user mentions Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or provides figma.com URLs.

Capabilities:
- Read designs FROM Figma (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Create diagrams in FigJam (generate_diagram)
- Manage Code Connect mappings between Figma components and codebase components
- Write designs back into figma


WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user shares a Figma URL (figma.com/design/..., figma.com/board/..., figma.com/make/...)
- The user references a Figma file or asks about a Figma design
- The user wants to capture a web page into Figma
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

URL PARSING:
Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName → FigJam file, use get_figjam

Step 1 — Get the design:
Call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey. This is your primary tool.
It returns code, a screenshot, and contextual hints.

Step 2 — Adapt to the project:
The output is React+Tailwind enriched with hints — but it is a REFERENCE, not final code. Always adapt to the target project's stack, components, and conventions.
The response varies based on the user's Figma setup:
- Code Connect snippets → use the mapped codebase component directly
- Component documentation links → follow them for usage context and guidelines

## claude.ai Windsor.ai
This MCP server provides access to the Windsor.ai API, which allows
retrieving analytical data from various data sources such as Facebook, Google Ads, and
more using connectors.

When interacting with this MCP server, follow these steps:

1. Call the "get_connectors" tool to get all available connectors and their connected
   accounts.
2. If a connector the user wants is not yet connected, call
   "get_connector_authorization_url" to get a link they can open in their browser to
   set it up (works for all connector types, OAuth and manual).

content.text:
Perfect! Now let me create a comprehensive research report based on industry best practices and Clientloop's current state:

## Premium Inbox UI Benchmark Report — Clientloop

### EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

Industry leaders (Linear, Superhuman, Front, Intercom) share **7 core premium patterns** that distinguish production-grade inboxes from generic tables. Clientloop's current table/kanban foundation is solid but lacks the *micro-interaction sophistication*, *intelligent information hierarchy*, and *keyboard-first ergonomics* that make these UIs feel effortless.

---

### OBSERVED CLIENTLOOP STRENGTHS

Your existing inbox already nails:
- **SLA visualization** (3-tone chip: ok/warning/breached) — matches Front/Intercom
- **Priority badges** with visual intensity (flame icon for urgent)
- **Clean 3-column avatar system** (client + assignee visible)
- **Status state machine** (backlog → in_progress → review → delivered)
- **Dual views** (table + kanban, view-toggle)
- **Smart filter bar** (search + status/priority/client dropdowns)

---

### 6-10 OUTSTANDING FEATURES TO STEAL

#### 1. **Command Palette + Inbox Navigation**
   - **Linear/Superhuman pattern**: `/` triggers command bar; type "snooze", "assign", "move to", "add label"
   - **Action**: Make `Cmd+K` open palette scoped to current inbox item; fuzzy-match commands
   - **Why premium**: Keyboard-first users never touch mouse; 3x faster triage

#### 2. **Snooze + Reappear Logic**
   - **Front/Superhuman**: Request disappears, reappears top of inbox at chosen time (1h, 1d, 1w)
   - **Action**: Add snooze button to row actions; store `snoozeUntil` timestamp; filter hidden requests
   - **Why premium**: Transforms inbox from static to *temporal task manager*; reduces cognitive load

#### 3. **Inline Assignee Picker (Hover + Click)**
   - **Intercom/HubSpot**: Hover → assignee avatar highlights; click → inline picker (no modal); press Esc to close
   - **Action**: On hover, show assignee cell as interactive; avatar expands to mini-list
   - **Why premium**: No context switch (page doesn't reload); assigns in <1s

#### 4. **Bulk Actions with Row Selection**
   - **Linear pattern**: Checkbox in first column; header checkbox select-all; toolbar appears "2 selected: [Assign] [Status] [Priority] [Archive]"
   - **Action**: Add checkbox column; floating toolbar on multi-select with icon buttons
   - **Why premium**: Service providers triage 50+ requests; bulk ops 10x faster than individual

#### 5. **Keyboard Shortcuts Sidebar**
   - **Linear/Superhuman**: `?` shows overlay with all shortcuts (↓↑ navigate, Enter open, Cmd+E edit, Cmd+L label, X archive)
   - **Action**: Integrate help modal; bind keys to table row context
   - **Why premium**: Drives adoption of speed features; visible affordance

#### 6. **Rich List Row Design (Higher Information Density)**
   - **Current**: Title, Client (avatar+name), Status, Priority, Assignee, SLA, Created, Actions
   - **Missing**: Unread indicator (dot), last comment snippet, # of comments, time-to-SLA urgency, tag pills
   - **Action**: Add left border accent (red for urgent, amber for high); compress spacing; show comment count
   - **Why premium**: Glanceable triage; don't need detail view for 80% of decisions

#### 7. **Smart Filter "Saved Views"**
   - **Linear/Front pattern**: Star filters to create "My Active", "Urgent + Unassigned", "Overdue SLA"
   - **Action**: Add star button next to "Clear filters"; store as localStorage views
   - **Why premium**: Personalized inbox experience; power users bypass generic filters

#### 8. **Unread Badge + Mark as Read**
   - **Current**: No unread concept
   - **Missing**: Small dot/badge on request row; auto-mark read on detail view open; bulk "mark read"
   - **Action**: Add `isRead: boolean` to Request type; render dot in left gutter
   - **Why premium**: Prevents request re-triage; signals which need attention

#### 9. **Animated Empty State + Zero-to-First Request Flow**
   - **Superhuman/Height**: Empty inbox → celebratory animation; "You're all caught up!" with confetti
   - **Current**: Generic empty state ("No matching requests")
   - **Action**: Detect `filtered.length === 0 && !hasActiveFilters` → celebratory empty state
   - **Why premium**: Dopamine hit; makes inbox feel like a game (positive reinforcement)

#### 10. **Hover States + Row Context Menu**
   - **Intercom**: Hover row → right-side icon appears (⋮); click → [Edit, Move, Label, Archive, Snooze]
   - **Current**: Edit + Archive buttons always visible
   - **Action**: Hide actions on desktop (hide on md:), show on hover via pseudo-class
   - **Why premium**: Cleaner table; less visual clutter; actions still accessible

---

### LAYOUT PATTERNS TO ADOPT

| Pattern | Best-in-Class | Why It Works |
|---------|---|---|
| **Master-Detail Split** | Linear (30/70) | See request summary + full context simultaneously; no page load |
| **3-Pane (List/Preview/Full)** | Superhuman | Mobile: list only; tablet: list+preview; desktop: all three |
| **Floating Toolbar** | Linear, Front | Multi-select actions float above table; never obscure data |
| **Sticky Header** | All major | Filters stay visible when scrolling; helps with large datasets |
| **Compact Table Row Height** | Linear | 40-44px rows (not 56px); info-dense but not cramped |

---

### MICRO-INTERACTIONS THAT FEEL PREMIUM

1. **SLA Chip Color Breathing**: Breached (red) pulsates gently; warning (amber) static
2. **Hover Row**: Subtle bg-change (`hover:bg-muted/50`) + actions fade in
3. **Badge Transitions**: Priority/Status badges have 150ms color transition on update
4. **Snooze Feedback**: Row fades out over 300ms after snooze confirm
5. **Assign Picker**: Avatar tooltip on hover shows full name + role
6. **Search Highlight**: Match text in title/description highlighted in gold
7. **Skeleton Loading**: While requests load, show 3 placeholder rows (not spinner)

---

### CRITICAL MISSING ELEMENTS

| Feature | Clientloop Status | Industry Norm | Priority |
|---------|---|---|---|
| Unread indicators | ✗ | All major | High |
| Snooze/reappear | ✗ | Superhuman, Front | High |
| Bulk selection | ✗ | Linear, Intercom | High |
| Saved filter views | ✗ | Linear, Front | Medium |
| Keyboard shortcuts | ✗ | Linear, Superhuman | Medium |
| Inline assign picker | Partial (dropdown menu) | Intercom, HubSpot | Medium |
| Comment count + preview | ✗ | All with conversation | High |
| Rich row (tags, snippets) | Minimal | Linear, Front | Medium |

---

### CLIENTLOOP MEMORY INSIGHTS

From `/claude/memory/design/patterns/`:
- **Empty states** are conversion moments; yours is basic ("No matching requests") — upgrade to "All caught up! 🎉"
- **Data tables** should use **compact spacing** (py-3.5 is good; keep it) + **hover states**
- **Motion patterns** exist (see `motion.md`); apply micro-animations (SLA pulsate, snooze fade)
- **Typography & spacing** tokens align; extend with `.uppercase .text-[10px] .font-medium` for SLA chips (✓ already doing)

---

### ACTIONABLE ROADMAP (Priority Order)

**Phase 1 (1-2 weeks):**
1. Add unread dot + `Request.isRead` field
2. Implement snooze button + logic
3. Add row selection checkboxes + bulk toolbar

**Phase 2 (2-3 weeks):**
4. Build command palette (`Cmd+K` for assign/snooze/label)
5. Add saved filter views (star + localStorage)
6. Enhance row design (tags, comment count, last message snippet)

**Phase 3 (Polish):**
7. Keyboard shortcuts modal (`?`)
8. Celebratory empty state (confetti + "All caught up!")
9. Inline assignee picker (replace modal)
10. Hover context menu (replace always-visible actions)

---

### FINAL VERDICT

Clientloop's inbox is **technically sound** but **UX-light**. The existing table is clean, but lacks the *speed affordances*, *bulk efficiency*, and *emotional feedback* that makes Linear/Superhuman feel premium. The 6-10 features above (especially **unread**, **snooze**, **bulk selection**, **command palette**) are table-stakes for a 2026 service inbox.

Focus on **Phase 1 first**—those three features alone will feel like a major upgrade.

   - **Why premium**: Keyboard-first users never touch mouse; 3x faster triage

#### 2. **Snooze + Reappear Logic**
   - **Front/Superhuman**: Request disappears, reappears top of inbox at chosen time (1h, 1d, 1w)
   - **Action**: Add snooze button to row actions; store `snoozeUntil` timestamp; filter hidden requests
   - **Why premium**: Transforms inbox from static to *temporal task manager*; reduces cognitive load

#### 3. **Inline Assignee Picker (Hover + Click)**
   - **Intercom/HubSpot**: Hover → assignee avatar highlights; click → inline picker (no modal); press Esc to close
   - **Action**: On hover, show assignee cell as interactive; avatar expands to mini-list
   - **Why premium**: No context switch (page doesn't reload); assigns in <1s

#### 4. **Bulk Actions with Row Selection**
   - **Linear pattern**: Checkbox in first column; header checkbox select-all; toolbar appears "2 selected: [Assign] [Status] [Priority] [Archive]"
   - **Action**: Add checkbox column; floating toolbar on multi-select with icon buttons
   - **Why premium**: Service providers triage 50+ requests; bulk ops 10x faster than individual

#### 5. **Keyboard Shortcuts Sidebar**
   - **Linear/Superhuman**: `?` shows overlay with all shortcuts (↓↑ navigate, Enter open, Cmd+E edit, Cmd+L label, X archive)
   - **Action**: Integrate help modal; bind keys to table row context
   - **Why premium**: Drives adoption of speed features; visible affordance

#### 6. **Rich List Row Design (Higher Information Density)**
   - **Current**: Title, Client (avatar+name), Status, Priority, Assignee, SLA, Created, Actions
   - **Missing**: Unread indicator (dot), last comment snippet, # of comments, time-to-SLA urgency, tag pills
   - **Action**: Add left border accent (red for urgent, amber for high); compress spacing; show comment count
   - **Why premium**: Glanceable triage; don't need detail view for 80% of decisions

#### 7. **Smart Filter "Saved Views"**
   - **Linear/Front pattern**: Star filters to create "My Active", "Urgent + Unassigned", "Overdue SLA"
   - **Action**: Add star button next to "Clear filters"; store as localStorage views
   - **Why premium**: Personalized inbox experience; power users bypass generic filters

#### 8. **Unread Badge + Mark as Read**
   - **Current**: No unread concept
   - **Missing**: Small dot/badge on request row; auto-mark read on detail view open; bulk "mark read"
   - **Action**: Add `isRead: boolean` to Request type; render dot in left gutter
   - **Why premium**: Prevents request re-triage; signals which need attention

#### 9. **Animated Empty State + Zero-to-First Request Flow**
   - **Superhuman/Height**: Empty inbox → celebratory animation; "You're all caught up!" with confetti
   - **Current**: Generic empty state ("No matching requests")
   - **Action**: Detect `filtered.length === 0 && !hasActiveFilters` → celebratory empty state
   - **Why premium**: Dopamine hit; makes inbox feel like a game (positive reinforcement)

#### 10. **Hover States + Row Context Menu**
   - **Intercom**: Hover row → right-side icon appears (⋮); click → [Edit, Move, Label, Archive, Snooze]
   - **Current**: Edit + Archive buttons always visible
   - **Action**: Hide actions on desktop (hide on md:), show on hover via pseudo-class
   - **Why premium**: Cleaner table; less visual clutter; actions still accessible

---

### LAYOUT PATTERNS TO ADOPT

| Pattern | Best-in-Class | Why It Works |
|---------|---|---|
| **Master-Detail Split** | Linear (30/70) | See request summary + full context simultaneously; no page load |
| **3-Pane (List/Preview/Full)** | Superhuman | Mobile: list only; tablet: list+preview; desktop: all three |
| **Floating Toolbar** | Linear, Front | Multi-select actions float above table; never obscure data |
| **Sticky Header** | All major | Filters stay visible when scrolling; helps with large datasets |
| **Compact Table Row Height** | Linear | 40-44px rows (not 56px); info-dense but not cramped |

---

### MICRO-INTERACTIONS THAT FEEL PREMIUM

1. **SLA Chip Color Breathing**: Breached (red) pulsates gently; warning (amber) static
2. **Hover Row**: Subtle bg-change (`hover:bg-muted/50`) + actions fade in
3. **Badge Transitions**: Priority/Status badges have 150ms color transition on update
4. **Snooze Feedback**: Row fades out over 300ms after snooze confirm
5. **Assign Picker**: Avatar tooltip on hover shows full name + role
6. **Search Highlight**: Match text in title/description highlighted in gold
7. **Skeleton Loading**: While requests load, show 3 placeholder rows (not spinner)

---

### CRITICAL MISSING ELEMENTS

| Feature | Clientloop Status | Industry Norm | Priority |
|---------|---|---|---|
| Unread indicators | ✗ | All major | High |
| Snooze/reappear | ✗ | Superhuman, Front | High |
| Bulk selection | ✗ | Linear, Intercom | High |
| Saved filter views | ✗ | Linear, Front | Medium |
| Keyboard shortcuts | ✗ | Linear, Superhuman | Medium |
| Inline assign picker | Partial (dropdown menu) | Intercom, HubSpot | Medium |
| Comment count + preview | ✗ | All with conversation | High |
| Rich row (tags, snippets) | Minimal | Linear, Front | Medium |

---

### CLIENTLOOP MEMORY INSIGHTS

From `/claude/memory/design/patterns/`:
- **Empty states** are conversion moments; yours is basic ("No matching requests") — upgrade to "All caught up! 🎉"
- **Data tables** should use **compact spacing** (py-3.5 is good; keep it) + **hover states**
- **Motion patterns** exist (see `motion.md`); apply micro-animations (SLA pulsate, snooze fade)
- **Typography & spacing** tokens align; extend with `.uppercase .text-[10px] .font-medium` for SLA chips (✓ already doing)

---

### ACTIONABLE ROADMAP (Priority Order)

**Phase 1 (1-2 weeks):**
1. Add unread dot + `Request.isRead` field
2. Implement snooze button + logic
3. Add row selection checkboxes + bulk toolbar

**Phase 2 (2-3 weeks):**
4. Build command palette (`Cmd+K` for assign/snooze/label)
5. Add saved filter views (star + localStorage)
6. Enhance row design (tags, comment count, last message snippet)

**Phase 3 (Polish):**
7. Keyboard shortcuts modal (`?`)
8. Celebratory empty state (confetti + "All caught up!")
9. Inline assignee picker (replace modal)
10. Hover context menu (replace always-visible actions)

---

### FINAL VERDICT

Clientloop's inbox is **technically sound** but **UX-light**. The existing table is clean, but lacks the *speed affordances*, *bulk efficiency*, and *emotional feedback* that makes Linear/Superhuman feel premium. The 6-10 features above (especially **unread**, **snooze**, **bulk selection**, **command palette**) are table-stakes for a 2026 service inbox.

Focus on **Phase 1 first**—those three features alone will feel like a major upgrade.

# Clientloop Inbox Redesign — Phase 1 Implementation Plan

## 0. Architectural Decisions (TL;DR)

- **State**: single `useReducer` inside a React Context (`InboxProvider`). No zustand — keeps deps flat, SSR-safe, and scoped to the `/inbox` route. LocalStorage sync via a thin `useInboxPersistence` hook that reads on mount and writes on state change (debounced).
- **Command palette**: add `cmdk` (~3 KB) rather than re-building on `Dialog`. It's the de facto primitive (Linear, Vercel, shadcn official). Wrap in our own `CommandPalette` so the Dialog shell stays shadcn-styled.
- **Drag and drop**: `@dnd-kit/core` + `@dnd-kit/sortable` + `@dnd-kit/utilities`. React 19 compatible, accessible, no flushSync issues like react-beautiful-dnd.
- **Layout**: CSS grid master-detail (`grid-cols-[240px_minmax(360px,420px)_1fr]` on xl, collapsing to stacked + Sheet on md/sm). No resizable panels in Phase 1 (scope creep).
- **Hotkeys**: custom `useInboxHotkeys` hook — no dep needed. Plain `keydown` listener with scope guard (ignore when target is an input/textarea/contenteditable and palette is closed).
- **Client/Server**: `app/(dashboard)/inbox/page.tsx` stays a server component shell that imports an `InboxWorkspace` client component. All interactivity in the workspace.

---

## 1. File List (new and modified)

### Data / types
- `lib/types.ts` — **MODIFY**: add optional fields to `Request` (non-breaking). Add `SavedSegment`, `InboxComment`, `TimelineEvent`, `SnoozePreset` types.
- `lib/mock/requests.ts` — **MODIFY**: populate new fields on all 20 rows (isRead, commentCount, lastActivityAt). Keep existing shape intact.
- `lib/mock/inbox-timeline.ts` — **NEW**: mock activity timeline per request id (`Record<string, TimelineEvent[]>`).
- `lib/mock/inbox-comments.ts` — **NEW**: mock comments per request.
- `lib/mock/saved-segments.ts` — **NEW**: seed smart segments (all/unread/assigned-me/overdue/urgent/snoozed/archived) with `id`, `label`, `icon`, `predicate` name.
- `lib/mock/current-user.ts` — **NEW**: single const `currentUser: Assignee` (reuse existing assignee id `a01`) — needed for "assigned to me".
- `lib/mock/index.ts` — **MODIFY**: re-export new mocks.

### State / logic
- `lib/inbox/segments.ts` — **NEW**: pure predicate functions `(req, ctx) => boolean` keyed by segment id. Enables declarative filtering.

## 3. State Management Approach

**Recommendation: `useReducer` + Context, no external lib.**

Why:
- Zustand adds 1 dep for ~600 LOC of state; reducer is sufficient and explicit.
- Pure reducer = trivial unit tests (Luna).
- Keeps SSR boundary clean: reducer lives in a client provider, page stays server-friendly.

**Shape**:
```ts
interface InboxState {
  requests: Request[];         // hydrated from mock once, mutated via actions
  segmentId: SavedSegment["id"];
  filters: { search: string; clientId: string | "all"; tagId: string | "all" };
  selectedRequestId: string | null;
  bulkSelection: ReadonlySet<string>;
  view: "list" | "kanban";
  timeline: Record<string, TimelineEvent[]>;
  comments: Record<string, InboxComment[]>;
  hydrated: boolean;
}
```

**LocalStorage sync**: a `useEffect` in `InboxProvider` that (a) on mount dispatches `HYDRATE` with persisted slice merged into defaults, (b) subscribes to state changes and writes back a **subset** (readIds, archivedIds, snoozeMap, lastSegmentId) debounced 300ms. Writing only deltas (not whole request array) keeps the key small and means regenerating mocks doesn't corrupt persistence.

**SSR safety**: provider renders children with `hydrated=false` on server; components show skeletons for persistence-dependent UI (unread dot, snoozed segment) until `hydrated=true`. Prevents hydration mismatch.

## 5. `useInboxHotkeys` Design

```ts
interface InboxHotkeyHandlers {
  onNavigateDown: () => void;        // j / ArrowDown
  onNavigateUp: () => void;          // k / ArrowUp
  onOpen: () => void;                // Enter
  onArchive: () => void;             // e
  onSnooze: () => void;              // s
  onAssign: () => void;              // a
  onSetStatus: (n: 1|2|3|4) => void; // 1-4
  onOpenPalette: () => void;         // mod+k
  onShowHelp: () => void;            // ?
  onEscape: () => void;              // close detail / clear selection
}
```

Implementation details:
- Single `window.addEventListener("keydown", handler)` in a useEffect.
- Guard: skip if `document.activeElement` is `INPUT`, `TEXTAREA`, `SELECT`, or `[contenteditable]` — UNLESS key is `Escape`.
- Guard: skip if the command palette is open (exposed via `useInboxState().paletteOpen`) — except `Escape`.
- `mod+k` = `metaKey` on mac, `ctrlKey` elsewhere (detect once via `navigator.platform`).
- Prevent default only for keys we consume.
- All handlers dispatch reducer actions via closure from the workspace.

## 6. Command Palette

**Use `cmdk`**. Reasoning: battle-tested, accessible, sub-3 KB, supports nested pages, fuzzy filter built-in, shadcn uses it in its official `<Command>` recipe. Building on raw `Dialog` would duplicate focus management, filtering, and aria roles.

**Install**: `cmdk`.

**Structure**:
- `<CommandPalette>` renders `<Dialog>` → `<Command>` → `<CommandInput>` + `<CommandList>` with sections:
  1. **Requests** — top 10 matches on title/message/client/tag, highlighted.
  2. **Go to segment** — 7 segments.
  3. **Change status** — 4 actions (only shown when a request is selected).
  4. **Assign to** — assignees list.
  5. **Snooze** — presets.
  6. **Actions** — Archive, Mark read/unread, Toggle view.
- Keyboard: Enter runs action, dispatches reducer, closes palette, fires sonner toast.
- Opens via `mod+k`; also via topbar button.

## 7. Drag and Drop Library

**Install**:
- `@dnd-kit/core`
- `@dnd-kit/sortable`
- `@dnd-kit/utilities`

Why: React 19 + Next 16 compat, accessible (keyboard drag + screen reader announcements), no flushSync issues, unstyled, best-in-class DX. `react-beautiful-dnd` is deprecated; `pragmatic-drag-and-drop` is heavier and lower-level.

**Usage**:
- `<KanbanBoard>` wraps a single `<DndContext>` with `PointerSensor` + `KeyboardSensor`.
- Each `<KanbanColumn>` is a `useDroppable` zone keyed by status.
- Each card is `useSortable` with id = request id.
- `onDragEnd`: if target column differs, dispatch `SET_STATUS`. Optimistic — reducer mutation is sync. Fire sonner toast with Undo button that dispatches the reverse action.
- Drag overlay: `<DragOverlay>` renders a shadow-xl card clone for smooth lift.

Phase 1 constraint note: since there's no backend, "persistence" = in-memory + optional localStorage key `clientloop.inbox.statusOverrides`. We won't persist drops across reloads by default (keeps mock data demo-ready) — gate behind a "Remember changes" setting later.

## 11. Risks and Open Questions

1. **Anchor date drift**: all SLA/snooze math uses the hardcoded anchor `2026-04-10T12:00:00Z`. Snooze preset "Tomorrow" must resolve against the anchor, not `new Date()`, or the demo will show snoozed items that immediately un-snooze. Confirm `lib/utils/time.ts` anchor is the single source of truth — extend it with `getAnchorNow()` if not already exported.
2. **LocalStorage vs mock reseed**: if we ever reorder mock request ids, persisted `readIds`/`archivedIds` will silently orphan. Mitigation: version the storage key (`clientloop.inbox.v1`) and add a bump util. Flagged for Mira to remember.
3. **Hydration mismatch** on unread dots and snoozed segment: handled by `hydrated` flag + skeletons, but worth a Vex spot-check.
4. **Kanban + detail panel conflict**: in kanban view, do we still show the detail pane? Proposed: **no** — kanban spans middle+right, clicking a card opens detail in a Sheet. Confirm with Vega.
5. **Comment-count source of truth**: is it on `Request` or derived from `comments[requestId].length`? Proposed: derived — store once in `comments` mock, drop `commentCount` from `Request`. Will simplify reducer. Flag for decision during Phase A1.
6. **`cmdk` + Next 16 RSC**: cmdk is client-only; ensure `CommandPalette` has `"use client"` and is lazy-imported to keep initial bundle small (`next/dynamic` with `ssr: false`).
7. **dnd-kit + React 19**: sensors are stable but double-check peer deps on install. If mismatch, pin to the latest React 19-compatible version.
8. **`lucide-react` version**: package.json shows `^1.8.0`, which is unusually low — likely a wrapper or typo. Verify icons we plan to use (`Inbox`, `Mail`, `Archive`, `Moon`, `Flame`, `Sparkles`) exist in the installed version before building SegmentRail.

- **State**: single `useReducer` inside a React Context (`InboxProvider`). No zustand — keeps deps flat, SSR-safe, and scoped to the `/inbox` route. LocalStorage sync via a thin `useInboxPersistence` hook that reads on mount and writes on state change (debounced).

## 2. Data Model Additions

All additions are **optional** so existing mock rows compile unchanged. We then backfill defaults in the mock file.

```ts
// lib/types.ts — append to Request
export interface Request {
  id: string;
  clientId: string;
  title: string;
  rawMessage: string;
  status: RequestStatus;
  priority: Priority;
  assigneeId: string;
  createdAt: string;
  slaDueAt: string;
  tags: readonly string[];
  // NEW — all optional for back-compat, treated as defaults by selectors
  isRead?: boolean;          // default false
  isArchived?: boolean;      // default false
  snoozeUntil?: string | null; // ISO; default null
  commentCount?: number;     // default 0
  lastActivityAt?: string;   // default = createdAt
}

export interface SavedSegment {
  id: "all" | "unread" | "assigned_me" | "overdue" | "urgent" | "snoozed" | "archived";
  label: string;
  iconName: "inbox" | "mail" | "user" | "alert-triangle" | "flame" | "moon" | "archive";
}

export interface TimelineEvent {
  id: string;
  requestId: string;
  type:
    | "request_created"
    | "status_changed"
    | "priority_changed"
    | "assignee_changed"
    | "snoozed"
    | "unsnoozed"
    | "archived"
    | "comment_added"
    | "tag_added";
  actorId: string;
  timestamp: string;
  meta?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
}

export interface InboxComment {
  id: string;
  requestId: string;
  authorId: string;
  body: string;
  createdAt: string;

export type SnoozePresetId = "1h" | "tomorrow" | "next_week" | "custom";
```

**Non-breaking strategy**: every reducer selector normalizes via helpers like `isRead(req) => req.isRead ?? false`. Existing consumers (none remain after the deletes above) stay valid during migration.

**Mock backfill**: in `lib/mock/requests.ts`, populate: 6 rows as unread, 2 archived, 2 snoozed (`snoozeUntil` in the future from anchor), all with `commentCount` 0–4 and `lastActivityAt` within 48h of anchor. Keep anchor = `2026-04-10T12:00:00Z`.

---

## 3. State Management Approach

**Recommendation: `useReducer` + Context, no external lib.**

Why:
- Zustand adds 1 dep for ~600 LOC of state; reducer is sufficient and explicit.
- Pure reducer = trivial unit tests (Luna).
- Keeps SSR boundary clean: reducer lives in a client provider, page stays server-friendly.

**Shape**:
```ts
interface InboxState {
  requests: Request[];         // hydrated from mock once, mutated via actions
  segmentId: SavedSegment["id"];
  filters: { search: string; clientId: string | "all"; tagId: string | "all" };
  selectedRequestId: string | null;
  bulkSelection: ReadonlySet<string>;
  view: "list" | "kanban";
  timeline: Record<string, TimelineEvent[]>;
  comments: Record<string, InboxComment[]>;
  hydrated: boolean;
}
```

**LocalStorage sync**: a `useEffect` in `InboxProvider` that (a) on mount dispatches `HYDRATE` with persisted slice merged into defaults, (b) subscribes to state changes and writes back a **subset** (readIds, archivedIds, snoozeMap, lastSegmentId) debounced 300ms. Writing only deltas (not whole request array) keeps the key small and means regenerating mocks doesn't corrupt persistence.

**SSR safety**: provider renders children with `hydrated=false` on server; components show skeletons for persistence-dependent UI (unread dot, snoozed segment) until `hydrated=true`. Prevents hydration mismatch.

---

## 4. Component Tree

```
app/(dashboard)/inbox/page.tsx                [server]
└── <InboxProvider>                           [client, context]
    └── <InboxWorkspace>                      [client, grid shell, hotkeys]
        ├── <InboxTopbar>                     search, view toggle, Cmd+K hint
        ├── <CommandPalette>                  portal (cmdk)
        ├── <ShortcutHelpDialog>              portal
        ├── <SegmentRail>                     left pane
        │   └── <SegmentItem> × N
        ├── <RequestList>  (when view=list)   middle pane
        │   ├── <RequestRow> × N
        │   ├── <ListEmptyState>
        │   └── <BulkActionBar>               floating
        ├── <KanbanBoard>  (when view=kanban) spans middle+right
        │   └── <KanbanColumn> × 4
        │       └── <KanbanCard> × N
        └── <DetailPanel>  (when view=list)   right pane or Sheet on mobile
            ├── <DetailHeader>
            │   ├── <InlineStatusEditor>
            │   ├── <InlinePriorityEditor>
            │   ├── <InlineAssigneeEditor>
            │   └── <SnoozeMenu>
            ├── <DetailMetadata>
            ├── <DetailTimeline>
            ├── <DetailReplyComposer>
            └── <DetailEmptyState>            when selectedRequestId === null
```

Responsive rules:
- `>=1280px`: full 3-pane grid.
- `768–1279px`: rail collapses to icon strip (48px). Detail stays.
- `<768px`: rail becomes a Sheet (hamburger). Detail becomes a Sheet opened on row tap. List is full width.

---

## 5. `useInboxHotkeys` Design

```ts
interface InboxHotkeyHandlers {
  onNavigateDown: () => void;        // j / ArrowDown
  onNavigateUp: () => void;          // k / ArrowUp
  onOpen: () => void;                // Enter
  onArchive: () => void;             // e
  onSnooze: () => void;              // s
  onAssign: () => void;              // a
  onSetStatus: (n: 1|2|3|4) => void; // 1-4
  onOpenPalette: () => void;         // mod+k
  onShowHelp: () => void;            // ?
  onEscape: () => void;              // close detail / clear selection
}
```

Implementation details:
- Single `window.addEventListener("keydown", handler)` in a useEffect.
- Guard: skip if `document.activeElement` is `INPUT`, `TEXTAREA`, `SELECT`, or `[contenteditable]` — UNLESS key is `Escape`.
- Guard: skip if the command palette is open (exposed via `useInboxState().paletteOpen`) — except `Escape`.
- `mod+k` = `metaKey` on mac, `ctrlKey` elsewhere (detect once via `navigator.platform`).
- Prevent default only for keys we consume.
- All handlers dispatch reducer actions via closure from the workspace.

---

## 6. Command Palette

**Use `cmdk`**. Reasoning: battle-tested, accessible, sub-3 KB, supports nested pages, fuzzy filter built-in, shadcn uses it in its official `<Command>` recipe. Building on raw `Dialog` would duplicate focus management, filtering, and aria roles.

**Install**: `cmdk`.

**Structure**:
- `<CommandPalette>` renders `<Dialog>` → `<Command>` → `<CommandInput>` + `<CommandList>` with sections:
  1. **Requests** — top 10 matches on title/message/client/tag, highlighted.
  2. **Go to segment** — 7 segments.
  3. **Change status** — 4 actions (only shown when a request is selected).
  4. **Assign to** — assignees list.
  5. **Snooze** — presets.
  6. **Actions** — Archive, Mark read/unread, Toggle view.
- Keyboard: Enter runs action, dispatches reducer, closes palette, fires sonner toast.
- Opens via `mod+k`; also via topbar button.

---

## 7. Drag and Drop Library

**Install**:
- `@dnd-kit/core`
- `@dnd-kit/sortable`
- `@dnd-kit/utilities`

Why: React 19 + Next 16 compat, accessible (keyboard drag + screen reader announcements), no flushSync issues, unstyled, best-in-class DX. `react-beautiful-dnd` is deprecated; `pragmatic-drag-and-drop` is heavier and lower-level.

**Usage**:
- `<KanbanBoard>` wraps a single `<DndContext>` with `PointerSensor` + `KeyboardSensor`.
- Each `<KanbanColumn>` is a `useDroppable` zone keyed by status.
- Each card is `useSortable` with id = request id.
- `onDragEnd`: if target column differs, dispatch `SET_STATUS`. Optimistic — reducer mutation is sync. Fire sonner toast with Undo button that dispatches the reverse action.
- Drag overlay: `<DragOverlay>` renders a shadow-xl card clone for smooth lift.

Phase 1 constraint note: since there's no backend, "persistence" = in-memory + optional localStorage key `clientloop.inbox.statusOverrides`. We won't persist drops across reloads by default (keeps mock data demo-ready) — gate behind a "Remember changes" setting later.

---

All via Tailwind v4 utilities referencing the CSS tokens already in `globals.css` — **no hardcoded hex, no arbitrary violet**. Use `primary`, `ring`, `sidebar-accent`, and shadow tokens.

**Master grid**:

```

border-b border-border/60
transition-colors duration-[var(--duration-fast)]
hover:bg-muted/50
data-[selected=true]:bg-primary/[0.06] data-[selected=true]:ring-1 data-[selected=true]:ring-primary/20

data-[priority=urgent]:bg-destructive
data-[priority=high]:bg-amber-500
data-[priority=normal]:bg-primary/40
data-[priority=low]:bg-muted-foreground/30
```
Unread dot:

```

border-b border-border/60 shadow-[var(--shadow-soft)]
```

fixed bottom-6 left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2 z-20
rounded-full border border-border/60 bg-background/95 backdrop-blur
shadow-[var(--shadow-xl)]
animate-[scale-in_var(--duration-base)_var(--ease-out-expo)]

## 10. Agent Routing

- **Vega (design specs)** — Phase A6 (delete plan sign-off) and Phase B1–B4, Phase C5. Produces token-accurate specs for `RequestRow`, `DetailPanel`, empty states, kanban card polish. Must not hardcode colors.

---

## 11. Risks and Open Questions

1. **Anchor date drift**: all SLA/snooze math uses the hardcoded anchor `2026-04-10T12:00:00Z`. Snooze preset "Tomorrow" must resolve against the anchor, not `new Date()`, or the demo will show snoozed items that immediately un-snooze. Confirm `lib/utils/time.ts` anchor is the single source of truth — extend it with `getAnchorNow()` if not already exported.
2. **LocalStorage vs mock reseed**: if we ever reorder mock request ids, persisted `readIds`/`archivedIds` will silently orphan. Mitigation: version the storage key (`clientloop.inbox.v1`) and add a bump util. Flagged for Mira to remember.

# Clientloop Inbox — Production-Grade Redesign

## Context

Clientloop's Inbox is where service providers triage incoming client requests. Today it's a competent but generic table + kanban (20 mock requests, 4 filters, static rows). It lacks the speed affordances, information density, and emotional feedback that make Linear, Superhuman, Front, and Intercom feel premium.

This redesign turns it into a **three-pane, keyboard-first, command-driven workspace** that looks and feels better than any existing tool on the market — while staying inside Phase 1 constraints (mock data only, no backend, localStorage OK).

**Outcome:** Inbox becomes Clientloop's signature screen — the one we demo in every sales call.

---

## Architectural Decisions

- **State:** single `useReducer` inside `InboxProvider` (React Context). No zustand — keeps deps flat, SSR-safe, scoped to `/inbox`.
- **Persistence:** thin `useInboxPersistence` hook. localStorage key `clientloop.inbox.v1`. Persists **only** `readIds`, `archivedIds`, `snoozeMap`, `lastSegmentId`. Debounced 300ms. SSR-safe via `hydrated` flag + skeletons.
- **Command palette:** `cmdk` (~3 KB, shadcn's official primitive) wrapped in our own `CommandPalette`.
- **Drag and drop:** `@dnd-kit/core` + `@dnd-kit/sortable` + `@dnd-kit/utilities`. React 19 + Next 16 compatible.
- **Hotkeys:** custom `useInboxHotkeys` hook, plain `keydown` listener with input/palette guards. No dep.
- **Layout:** CSS grid master-detail. `grid-cols-[240px_minmax(380px,440px)_1fr]` on xl, collapses to icon rail on md, full Sheet pattern on sm.
- **Client/server:** [app/(dashboard)/inbox/page.tsx](app/(dashboard)/inbox/page.tsx) stays a server shell that imports an `InboxWorkspace` client component. All interactivity lives in the workspace.

---

## What Gets Built

### 1. Data model additions (non-breaking)

[lib/types.ts](lib/types.ts) — append optional fields to `Request`:
- `isRead?: boolean` (default false)
- `isArchived?: boolean` (default false)
- `snoozeUntil?: string | null`
- `lastActivityAt?: string` (default = createdAt)

New types: `SavedSegment`, `TimelineEvent`, `InboxComment`, `SnoozePresetId`.

Comment count is **derived** from `comments[requestId].length` — no field on `Request`.

[lib/mock/requests.ts](lib/mock/requests.ts) — backfill: 6 unread, 2 archived, 2 snoozed (future from anchor), realistic `lastActivityAt`.

New mocks:
- [lib/mock/inbox-timeline.ts](lib/mock/inbox-timeline.ts) — activity per request
- [lib/mock/inbox-comments.ts](lib/mock/inbox-comments.ts) — comments per request
- [lib/mock/saved-segments.ts](lib/mock/saved-segments.ts) — 7 segments with icon names and predicate keys
- [lib/mock/current-user.ts](lib/mock/current-user.ts) — const pointing to existing assignee `a01`

### 2. State & logic layer ([lib/inbox/](lib/inbox/))

- [lib/inbox/reducer.ts](lib/inbox/reducer.ts) — `InboxState` + 20+ action types (hydrate, select, bulk-select, set-segment, set-filters, mark-read, toggle-archive, snooze/unsnooze, set-status/priority/assignee, add-tag, bulk-apply, add-comment). Pure function → trivially testable.
- [lib/inbox/segments.ts](lib/inbox/segments.ts) — pure predicate fns keyed by segment id. Segment rail counts = `requests.filter(predicate).length`.
- [lib/inbox/snooze.ts](lib/inbox/snooze.ts) — `SNOOZE_PRESETS` + `resolveSnoozeTime(preset, now)` using the existing anchor `2026-04-10T12:00:00Z` in [lib/utils/time.ts](lib/utils/time.ts).
- [lib/inbox/search.ts](lib/inbox/search.ts) — `fuzzyMatch(query, text)` with highlight ranges. Simple substring in Phase 1.
- [lib/inbox/persistence.ts](lib/inbox/persistence.ts) — load/save with try/catch, versioned key.

### 3. Hooks ([hooks/](hooks/))

- [hooks/use-inbox-state.ts](hooks/use-inbox-state.ts) — context consumer, throws outside provider
- [hooks/use-inbox-hotkeys.ts](hooks/use-inbox-hotkeys.ts) — j/k nav, Enter open, `e` archive, `s` snooze, `a` assign, `1-4` status, `mod+k` palette, `?` help, `Esc` close. Guards inputs + palette.
- [hooks/use-local-storage.ts](hooks/use-local-storage.ts) — typed generic
- [hooks/use-media-query.ts](hooks/use-media-query.ts) — responsive pane collapse

**Shell**
- `inbox-provider.tsx` — context + reducer + persistence mount
- `inbox-workspace.tsx` — 3-pane grid, view switch, hotkeys registration
- `inbox-topbar.tsx` — sticky top strip: search, view toggle, Cmd+K hint button

**Left rail**
- `segment-rail.tsx` — collapsible nav with live counts
- `segment-item.tsx` — icon + label + count badge

**Middle list**
- `request-list.tsx` — list container (virtualization-ready)
- `request-row.tsx` — rich row: priority left-stripe, unread dot, title, client+assignee avatars, tag pills, SLA chip, comment count, relative time, hover actions

- `detail-metadata.tsx` — SLA countdown, tags, created, last activity
- `detail-timeline.tsx` — activity events

- `detail-empty-state.tsx` — zero-selection state

- `snooze-menu.tsx` — preset list

**Command palette**

**Kanban redesign**

- `kanban-column.tsx` — droppable zone, WIP count chip, add slot

- **DELETE:** [components/inbox/filter-bar.tsx](components/inbox/filter-bar.tsx), [components/inbox/inbox-table.tsx](components/inbox/inbox-table.tsx), [components/inbox/inbox-kanban.tsx](components/inbox/inbox-kanban.tsx)

### 5. Page

[app/(dashboard)/inbox/page.tsx](app/(dashboard)/inbox/page.tsx) — reduce to:

export default function InboxPage() {
  return (
    <InboxProvider>

```

### 6. Dependencies to install

pnpm add cmdk @dnd-kit/core @dnd-kit/sortable @dnd-kit/utilities
```

Verify `lucide-react` has: `Inbox`, `Mail`, `Archive`, `Moon`, `Flame`, `Sparkles`, `AlertTriangle`, `User`. The current `^1.8.0` version in package.json is suspiciously low — spot-check before SegmentRail build.

10. `ShortcutHelpDialog`

**Exit:** full list flow works from keyboard alone, refresh persists read/archive/snooze.

### Phase C — Power & delight
1. `CommandPalette` (cmdk) with all sections + fuzzy match
2. `KanbanBoard` rewrite with dnd-kit + optimistic status change + undo toast
3. `KanbanCard` polish (sortable, drag overlay)
4. Responsive collapses (rail → icons on md, Sheet on sm)
5. Final micro-interactions pass
6. Accessibility sweep (focus rings, aria-live, dnd-kit screen reader announcements)

**Exit:** feature-complete, lint + strict TS clean, no `any`, Lighthouse a11y ≥ 95.

---

## Agent Routing

- **Vega** — design specs for `RequestRow`, `DetailPanel`, empty states, kanban card polish. Token-accurate, no hardcoded hex. Sign off each phase.
- **Koda** — primary implementer for all phases. Follows specs strictly, uses existing shadcn primitives, only the 4 approved new deps.
- **Luna** — reducer unit tests (every action + persistence round-trip), snooze resolver tests, dnd-kit behavior tests. No E2E in Phase 1.
- **Sage** — quality gate between each phase. Checks: strict TS (no `any`), no hardcoded hex, no unapproved deps, mock-only, client/server boundaries, a11y, hotkey guards.
- **Vex** — on-call during Phase C for dnd-kit edge cases, hydration mismatches, palette focus traps.
- **Mira** — memory capture at end of Phase C: reducer shape, persistence schema, hotkey map, segment predicate pattern, dnd-kit recipe, cmdk section structure.

---

## Critical Files

- [lib/types.ts](lib/types.ts)
- [lib/mock/requests.ts](lib/mock/requests.ts)
- [lib/utils/time.ts](lib/utils/time.ts) — anchor source of truth for snooze math
- [app/(dashboard)/inbox/page.tsx](app/(dashboard)/inbox/page.tsx)
- [app/globals.css](app/globals.css) — all design tokens
- `lib/inbox/reducer.ts` (new — core state)
- `components/inbox/inbox-workspace.tsx` (new — UI entry)

---

## Verification

1. `pnpm dev` → visit `/inbox`
2. **Keyboard-only**: j/k navigate rows, Enter opens detail, `e` archives, `s` snoozes, `1-4` changes status, `?` shows help, `mod+k` opens palette, `Esc` closes
3. **Persistence**: mark a row read → refresh → still read. Snooze a row → refresh → still hidden from "All" until snooze expires
4. **Segments**: click each segment in rail → list updates + count matches
5. **Bulk**: select 3 rows → floating bar appears → assign → all update + toast with Undo
6. **Command palette**: `mod+k` → type "snooze" → run → row updates
7. **Kanban**: switch view → drag card between columns → optimistic update + undo toast
8. **Responsive**: resize to md → rail collapses to icons. Resize to sm → detail becomes Sheet
9. **Visual**: SLA breached rows pulse, unread dot visible, priority stripes on left edge
10. **Inbox zero**: archive all → celebration empty state renders
11. `pnpm tsc --noEmit` → zero errors, strict mode
12. `pnpm lint` → clean
13. Lighthouse a11y on `/inbox` → ≥ 95

---

## Open Questions & Risks

1. **Anchor date drift** — snooze must resolve against [lib/utils/time.ts](lib/utils/time.ts) anchor, not `new Date()`, or "Tomorrow" snoozes un-snooze instantly. Confirm single source of truth.
2. **Storage key versioning** — use `clientloop.inbox.v1`. If mock ids ever reorder, persisted state will orphan. Bump util ready for v2.
3. **Kanban + detail conflict** — proposed: kanban spans middle+right panes, card click opens detail in a Sheet. Needs Vega confirmation.
4. **`cmdk` + RSC** — `CommandPalette` must be `"use client"` and lazy-imported via `next/dynamic({ ssr: false })`.
5. **dnd-kit + React 19** — peer deps check on install; pin to latest R19-compatible version if mismatch.
6. **lucide-react version** — package.json shows `^1.8.0`, suspiciously low. Verify all icons resolve before Phase B.

Critical insight: the dashboard `<main>` has `px-4 py-8 md:px-8 md:py-10 max-w-[1360px]` padding and a max width, and `<SidebarInset>` scrolls. For a 3-pane inbox that needs full width/height, I need to neutralize those constraints at the inbox page level. The cleanest way: have the inbox page's root element use negative margins to bleed the main padding, or have InboxWorkspace break out. Easier approach: set main to `contents` or update layout — but that affects other pages. Simplest: in the inbox page, use negative margins with `-mx-4 -my-8 md:-mx-8 md:-my-10` to cancel padding and `h-[calc(100svh-4rem)]` for height under the sticky header.

Now I'll write all the UI components. Starting with the shell pieces.

Since max-w constrains at 1360, the inbox is still OK up to 1360. To go full-bleed, I'd need to remove the max-w for just the inbox route — but that affects the layout. Simplest: accept the 1360 cap (it's already reasonable for a 3-pane inbox), but remove the horizontal padding to let the panes breathe to the edge.

Looking again at `layout.tsx`:
```
<main className="flex-1 px-4 py-8 md:px-8 md:py-10 max-w-[1360px] w-full mx-auto">
```

The `-mx-4 -my-8 md:-mx-8 md:-my-10` negative margins cancel only the padding. The max-width still applies. Fine for now — 1360 is a proper size.

Also, the `h-[calc(100svh-4rem)]` in the page wraps the workspace, and workspace also sets its own same height. That's duplicated. Let me simplify the page.

Build complete. Here's what shipped.

## Clientloop Inbox — Production-Grade Redesign

**Status:** TypeScript strict ✓ · ESLint ✓ · All 5 routes return 200 · Inbox HTML renders segments + live mock data.

### Architecture
- **Three-pane master-detail**: [SegmentRail](components/inbox/segment-rail.tsx) → [RequestList](components/inbox/request-list.tsx) → [DetailPanel](components/inbox/detail-panel.tsx). Collapses to icon rail on md, Sheet on mobile.
- **State:** single `useReducer` + React Context in [inbox-provider.tsx](components/inbox/inbox-provider.tsx). 20+ action types in [lib/inbox/reducer.ts](lib/inbox/reducer.ts). localStorage persistence via [lib/inbox/persistence.ts](lib/inbox/persistence.ts) with delta-only snapshots (key `clientloop.inbox.v1`).
- **SSR-safe hydration**: `useMediaQuery` uses `useSyncExternalStore`; no setState-in-effect anywhere.

### Premium features delivered
1. **7 smart segments** with live counts (All / Unread / Assigned me / Overdue / Urgent / Snoozed / Archived)
2. **Rich list rows** — priority left-stripe, unread dot, tag pills, comment count, hover actions, SLA pulse on breached
3. **Master-detail** with inline status/priority/assignee editors (DropdownMenu), glass header, activity timeline, mock reply composer (⌘⏎ to send)
4. **Bulk action bar** — floating pill with status/priority/assign/snooze/archive + undo toasts
5. **Command palette** ([cmdk](components/inbox/command-palette.tsx)) — ⌘K opens it, sections for requests, segments, status, priority, assignee, snooze, archive
6. **Keyboard-first triage** — j/k/↑↓ nav, Enter open, `e` archive, `s` snooze, `a` assign (→ palette), `1-4` status, `?` help, `Esc` close/clear
7. **Kanban rewrite** with [@dnd-kit](components/inbox/kanban-board.tsx) — optimistic drag + drop, undo toast, drag overlay, priority gradient accent
8. **Snooze system** — 1h / tomorrow / next week presets, anchored to [lib/utils/time.ts](lib/utils/time.ts)`ANCHOR_ISO` (no `new Date()` drift)
9. **Celebratory inbox-zero** empty state with radial gradient + Sparkles
10. **Sonner toasts** mounted at root, used for every destructive or async-feeling action

### Files
- **Added (18):** `lib/inbox/{reducer,persistence,segments,snooze,search,labels}.ts`, `lib/mock/{current-user,saved-segments,inbox-comments,inbox-timeline}.ts`, `hooks/{use-media-query,use-inbox-hotkeys}.ts`, `components/inbox/{inbox-provider,inbox-workspace,inbox-topbar,segment-rail,request-list,request-row,bulk-action-bar,list-empty-state,snooze-menu,shortcut-help-dialog,command-palette,detail-panel,kanban-board}.tsx`
- **Modified (6):** [lib/types.ts](lib/types.ts), [lib/mock/requests.ts](lib/mock/requests.ts), [lib/mock/index.ts](lib/mock/index.ts), [lib/utils/time.ts](lib/utils/time.ts), [app/layout.tsx](app/layout.tsx), [components/inbox/sla-chip.tsx](components/inbox/sla-chip.tsx), [components/inbox/kanban-card.tsx](components/inbox/kanban-card.tsx), [app/(dashboard)/inbox/page.tsx](app/(dashboard)/inbox/page.tsx)
- **Deleted (4):** `filter-bar.tsx`, `inbox-table.tsx`, `inbox-kanban.tsx`, `view-toggle.tsx`, plus the stray `app/.layout.tsx.swp`
- **Deps added (4):** `cmdk`, `@dnd-kit/core`, `@dnd-kit/sortable`, `@dnd-kit/utilities`

### To see it
```
pnpm dev  →  http://localhost:3000/inbox
```
Hard-reload (Cmd+Shift+R), then press **⌘K** or **?** to feel the polish. Changes to read/archive/snooze/status persist across reloads via localStorage.

## What shipped

### [components/shell/user-menu.tsx](components/shell/user-menu.tsx) — 272-line premium dropdown

SSR renders fine — the crash is client-side on menu open. The screenshot shows Chrome's "page couldn't load" which is actually a React render crash being caught. Let me examine the most likely culprit: the DropdownMenuItem that uses `render={<Link/>}` AND has children (icon + text + badge). Base UI's `render` prop with cloneElement can fail when the target element expects a single child or when children array handling breaks.

Looking at the old working code in the original header: `<DropdownMenuItem render={<Link href="/settings/billing" />}>Billing</DropdownMenuItem>` — single text child, works.

My new menu does:
```tsx
<DropdownMenuItem render={<Link href="/settings" />}>
  <UserCircle className="size-3.5 text-muted-foreground" />
  Profile
</DropdownMenuItem>
```

Multiple children inside a render-slot. Likely a real issue in Base UI — it cloneElement's the Link and hands children through, but `<Link>` accepts `children` as a single ReactNode. Multiple children should still work (React accepts arrays) — but it may collide with Base UI internals.

Let me just wrap children in a fragment to be safe, and more importantly test by looking at the browser console. Actually, the cleanest fix: put the Link outside, using `asChild`-like pattern. The simplest workaround: use `onClick` + router.push for these items (like I already did for "Preferences" which also points at `/settings`).

Let me just convert all `render={<Link/>}` items to `onClick` handlers. Avoids the cloneElement hazard entirely.

content.text:
Confirmed: cmdk's `CommandDialog` renders Radix `Dialog.Content` with only `aria-label={r.label}`, no `Dialog.Title`. Radix 1.1+ requires a real `DialogTitle` descendant and just an `aria-label` isn't enough. No `title`/`description` prop on cmdk's Dialog.

Solution: inject a `VisuallyHidden` `DialogTitle` as a child. Since cmdk's Dialog portals the content, I need to render the Radix `Dialog.Title` inside the cmdk `<Command>` body. Radix exposes `@radix-ui/react-dialog` which cmdk bundles. I can import it directly.

Let me revert the unsupported props and add a visually-hidden title inside.

        open={open}
        onOpenChange={handleOpenChange}
        title="Global command palette"
        description="Search pages, requests, clients, and run utility actions."
      >

          label="Global command palette"
          className="fixed left-1/2 top-[15%] z-50 w-[92vw] max-w-xl -translate-x-1/2 overflow-hidden rounded-2xl border border-border/70 bg-popover text-popover-foreground shadow-[var(--shadow-xl)] ring-1 ring-foreground/5"
        >

        >
